overall: The AG found the Cambridge City Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by withholding eight sets of litigation executive session minutes until the Monteiro-related settlement was fully performed in January 2012; the complaint against the city clerk individually was declined, and no order was issued.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Council unlawfully withheld minutes of eight executive sessions on a lawsuit, claiming release would harm the city's litigating position.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we fmd that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by withholding the minutes from these eight meetings until January 2012.

allegations.summary: Whether the executive session purpose (litigation) lawfully continued until the minutes were released in January 2012, after the August 2011 decision not to appeal.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by determining that the executive session purpose continued until January 2012, when all the terms of the settlement agreement had been performed.

allegations.summary: Complaint also named a city clerk individually as a respondent for the minutes withholding.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, we note that individuals who are not members of public bodies are not required to comply with the Open Meeting Law, therefore we decline to review the complaint against Ms. Drury, and only consider her actions to the extent they relate to the allegations against the Council.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
